# FAQ-008 Engineering FAQ #8

Revision: Rev A

Question: What lubricant should be used for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) and why?
Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-611 for EQ-P3-L3-CN02. Rationale: this formulation was selected during the last tooling qualification for turning operations because it balances film strength and washout resistance for our high-feed carbide inserts in this machine configuration. Background: the machine receives mixed ferrous and alloy workpieces and the lubricant must be compatible with downstream cleaning and heat treat processes. Example use case: when running continuous turning on long runs where surface finish retention is required, CFW-LUB-611 has shown improved tool life compared to general-purpose shop oils. Records to keep: log the part number used on the job traveler, note batch code of the lubricant dispenser, and attach a sampling result to the maintenance record for EQ-P3-L3-CN02. See ECN-2026-013 for the change notice that authorized the current lubricant selection and SOP-P1-L4-03 for the machine lubrication procedure.

Question: What lubricant should be used for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L2-RR01) and what special handling is required?
Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-961 for EQ-P1-L2-RR01. Rationale: ring rolling requires a high-pressure boundary lubricant with anti-stick properties to prevent smearing on the mandrel and to maintain surface integrity of the thin wall sections produced. Background: radial ring rolling imposes sliding contact at high contact pressures and this lubricant reduces the risk of surface defects. Special handling: store CFW-LUB-961 in a dedicated, labeled dispenser to prevent cross-contamination and use dedicated filling tools for the ring rolling system. Records to keep: include the dispenser refill date and operator initials in the lubrication log, and retain a sample certificate of analysis with the RR01 maintenance file. Refer to SB-1043 for ring rolling surface defect guidance and to ECN-2026-013 for the approved material list.

Question: What lubricant should be used for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) and are there downstream compatibility concerns?
Answer: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-477 for EQ-P1-L4-CN01. Rationale: heat treat shop machining requires lubricants that are compatible with furnace loading and that do not introduce residues that affect austenitizing or quench behavior. Background: the heat treat area has classification and inspection constraints for residues; CFW-LUB-477 meets those constraints and has been validated for ease of removal during standard cleaning prior to furnace entry. Compatibility note: always confirm that the lubricant batch certificate is present and that no additives have been introduced that are outside the approved specification for the heat treat line. Records to keep: attach lubricant batch certificate and cleaning verification to the furnace load paperwork for parts processed from EQ-P1-L4-CN01. See SOP-P1-L4-03 for cleaning and furnace loading steps.

Question: What austenitizing setpoint should be used for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) and how should it be documented?
Answer: The austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 is 885 °C. Rationale: this setpoint was selected to achieve the required transformation for the specified alloy family while maintaining grain control per material specification. Background: setpoint adherence must be verified with calibrated thermocouple data and certified chart or digital record. Documentation: record the setpoint as part of the heat treat cycle sheet, capture temperature profile traces for each furnace load, and archive the profile with the job lot file. Records to keep: retain the furnace profile, operator start and stop signatures, and any deviation notes in the heat treat batch record. See ECN-2026-013 for the authorization of the setpoint and SOP-P1-L4-03 for the heat treat recording procedure.

Question: What is the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02) and what monitoring is required?
Answer: The coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is 55 L/min. Rationale: induction coil cooling must maintain sufficient flow to prevent localized overheating and premature coil failure; the minimum was determined based on coil geometry and power loading. Monitoring: continuous flow indication is required at the operator station and interlock thresholds must be set to prevent operation below the minimum. Actions on low flow: operators must halt the heater feed and tag out the circuit until flow is restored to at least the specified minimum and the system is inspected for blockage or pump issues. Records to keep: log flow readings per shift, record any trips or interlock events, and file corrective action documentation with the equipment maintenance log for EQ-P2-L1-IH02. Refer to SB-1043 for failure modes related to coil cooling and to SOP-P1-L4-03 for the procedure to verify cooling systems prior to production start.

Related documents: ECN-2026-013, SB-1043, SOP-P1-L4-03.
